translations.literal: Third month, day jiaxu, edict: Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, jiaxu: the Ministry of Rites examinations were ordered.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲子，吳育卒。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiazi: Wu Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, jiazi: Wu Yu died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，罷睦親宅祖宗神御殿。

translations.literal: Day yichou: the ancestral spirit halls at the Muqin mansion were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the Muqin mansion ancestral spirit halls were closed.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔：「守令或貪恣耄昏，以弛為寬，以苛為察，以增賦斂為勞，以出入刑罰為能，而部使者莫之舉劾。

translations.literal: Day bingchen, edict: “Some prefects and magistrates are greedy, willful, senile, or muddled—treating laxness as leniency, harshness as scrutiny, tax increases as merit, and manipulating punishments as ability—yet circuit commissioners do not impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the throne rebuked greedy or muddled magistrates whom circuit commissioners failed to impeach.

sentences.zh: 自今其各思率職，毋撓權幸，毋縱有罪，以稱朕意。

translations.literal: From now on each should think how to perform his duty, not obstruct the powerful and favored, and not indulge the guilty, to accord with Our intent.”
translations.idiomatic: They were told to do their duty, not shield the powerful or indulge criminals.

sentences.zh: 」五月壬申，增國子監生員。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day renshen: National University student quotas were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, renshen: National University enrollment was raised.

sentences.zh: 甲午，契丹遣使致其祖母遺留物。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: the Khitan sent envoys bearing their grandmother’s bequest.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Liao envoys delivered their empress dowager’s bequest.

sentences.zh: 六月丙午，文彥博、賈昌朝罷，以富弼為昭文館大學士，韓琦同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士，宋庠、田況為樞密使，張昪為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day bingwu: Wen Yanbo and Jia Changchao were removed; Fu Bi was made Zhaowen grand academician; Han Qi associate chief councilor and Jixian grand academician; Song Qi and Tian Kuang military affairs commissioners; Zhang Bian vice military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, bingwu: Wen Yanbo and Jia Changchao fell; Fu Bi took Zhaowen; Han Qi joined the council; Song Qi and Tian Kuang headed Military Affairs; Zhang Bian became deputy.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔學士院編國朝制誥。

translations.literal: Day jiayin, edict: the Hanlin Academy was to compile the dynasty’s edicts and orders.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Hanlin was ordered to compile dynastic edicts.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，交阯貢異獸。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: Jiaozhi presented exotic beasts.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Jiaozhi sent exotic animals.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙子，詔廣濟河溢，原武縣河決，遣官行視民田，振恤被水害者。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day bingzi, edict: the Guangji Canal overflowed and the Yellow River burst at Yuanwu county; officials were sent to inspect farmland and relieve flood victims.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, bingzi: Guangji flooding and a Yuanwu breach brought inspectors to aid flood victims.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以夔州路旱，遣使安撫。

translations.literal: Day guisi: because Kuizhou circuit suffered drought, envoys were sent to comfort and soothe.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Kuizhou’s drought brought comfort envoys.

sentences.zh: 八月己亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jihai new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, new moon jihai: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 己未，王堯臣卒。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: Wang Yaochan died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Wang Yaochan died.

sentences.zh: 庚申，彭仕羲率眾降。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: Peng Shixi led his followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Peng Shixi surrendered with his men.

sentences.zh: 九月癸酉，議罷榷茶法。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day guiyou: abolition of the tea monopoly was debated.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, guiyou: ending the tea monopoly was debated.

sentences.zh: 己丑，契丹遣使來謝。

translations.literal: Day jichou: Khitan envoys came to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Liao envoys came to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸亥，除河北坊郭客戶乾食鹽錢。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guihai: dry-salt fees for Hebei urban client households were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, guihai: Hebei urban clients were freed from dry-salt fees.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸酉，議減冗費。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day guiyou: reduction of redundant expenses was debated.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, guiyou: cutting redundant spending was debated.

sentences.zh: 己丑，置都水監，罷三司河渠司。

translations.literal: Day jichou: the Directorate of Waterways was established; the Three Departments River Office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the Directorate of Waterways replaced the Three Departments River Office.

sentences.zh: 十二月己巳，詔三司歲上天下稅賦之數，三歲一會虧贏以聞。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jisi, edict: the Three Departments were annually to report nationwide tax receipts; every three years profit and loss were to be reconciled and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jisi: the Three Departments were to report annual taxes and triennial balances.

sentences.zh: 閏月丁卯朔，詔：「吏人及伎術官職，毋得任知州軍、提點刑獄，自軍班出至正任者，方得知邊要州軍。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day dingmao new moon, edict: “Clerks and technical specialists may not serve as prefects or punishments intendants; only those promoted from the military roster to regular office may govern key frontier prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, new moon dingmao: clerks and technicians were barred from prefectures and judicial posts; only promoted military officers could hold frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 」丁丑，詔裁定制科及進士高第人恩數。

translations.literal: ” Day dingchou, edict: trim the favors granted to classical-examination and high-ranking jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, favors for policy-exam and top jinshi graduates were trimmed.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔明年正旦日食，其自丁亥避正殿，減常膳。

translations.literal: Day gengchen, edict: because there would be a solar eclipse at New Year’s Day next year, from dinghai the main hall was avoided and regular meals reduced.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, next New Year’s eclipse ordered avoiding the main hall and cutting meals from dinghai.

sentences.zh: 宴契丹使，毋作樂。

translations.literal: When entertaining Khitan envoys, music was not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Liao envoys were entertained without music.

sentences.zh: 壬午，錄系囚，降三京囚罪一等，徒以下釋之。

translations.literal: Day renwu: prisoners were reviewed; crimes of prisoners in the three capitals were reduced one degree; penal servants and below were released.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, three-capital prisoners were cut one grade and penal servants freed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，安化上中下州、北遐鎮蠻人來貢。

translations.literal: That year, Anhua upper, middle, and lower prefectures and Beixia town barbarians came to tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Anhua and Beixia tribes sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月丙申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Year four, spring, first month, day bingshen new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 4, first month, new moon bingshen: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 用牲於社。

translations.literal: Victims were offered at the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were sacrificed at the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，御正殿，復常膳。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: the emperor held court in the main hall and regular meals were restored.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the court returned to the main hall and normal meals.

sentences.zh: 以自冬雨雪不止，遣官分行京城，賜孤窮老疾錢，畿縣委令佐為糜粥濟饑。

translations.literal: Because snow and rain had not ceased since winter, officials were sent through the capital to grant cash to the orphaned, destitute, aged, and ill; in capital counties magistrates and assistants were charged to give porridge relief to the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Endless winter rain sent officials to aid the capital poor; nearby counties served famine porridge.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，賜在京諸軍班緡錢。

translations.literal: Day renyin: cash was granted to capital army companies.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, capital garrison companies received cash.

sentences.zh: 頒《嘉祐驛令》。

translations.literal: The Jiayou Relay Statutes were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiayou Relay Statutes were issued.

sentences.zh: 二月己巳，罷榷茶。

translations.literal: Second month, day jisi: the tea monopoly was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, jisi: the tea monopoly ended.

sentences.zh: 庚午，廣南言交阯寇欽州。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: Guangnan reported that Jiaozhi raided Qin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Guangnan reported Jiaozhi raiding Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以廣惠倉隸司農寺。

translations.literal: Day yihai: the Broad Relief Granary was placed under the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the Broad Relief Granary was assigned to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 戊子，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: a white rainbow spanned the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, a white rainbow crossed the sun.

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，命近臣同三司減定民間科率。

translations.literal: Third month, day wuxu: close ministers were ordered jointly with the Three Departments to reduce and fix popular levies.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, wuxu: intimate ministers and the Three Departments were to cut popular levies.

sentences.zh: 是月，賜進士、諸科及第出身三百三十九人。

translations.literal: That month, three hundred thirty-nine jinshi and miscellaneous subjects who passed were granted rank.
translations.idiomatic: That month 339 jinshi and other graduates received rank.

sentences.zh: 五月戊戌，詔：「兩制臣僚舊制不許詣執政私第，所舉薦不得用為御史，今除其法。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuxu, edict: “Drafting officials were formerly forbidden to visit chief ministers’ private residences, and their recommendations could not be used for censor posts; these rules are now abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, wuxu: drafting officials could again visit chancellors privately and their nominees could become censors.

sentences.zh: 」庚子，詔內臣員多，權罷進養子入內。

translations.literal: ” Day gengzi, edict: because inner eunuchs were numerous, adoption of foster sons into the palace was temporarily suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, inner eunuch ranks were full and palace adoption of foster sons was suspended.

sentences.zh: 壬子，遣官經界河北牧地，餘募民種藝。

translations.literal: Day renzi: officials were sent to survey Hebei pasture lands; the remainder was opened to popular cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Hebei pastures were surveyed and surplus land opened to farmers.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，群臣請加尊號曰「大仁至治」，表五上，不許。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jisi: the ministers five times memorialized to add the honorific “Great Benevolence and Perfect Governance”; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, jisi: five petitions for the title “Great Benevolence and Perfect Governance” were refused.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔諸路經略安撫、轉運使、提點刑獄各舉本部官有行實政事者三人，以備升擢。

translations.literal: Day guiyou, edict: each circuit pacification commissioner, transport commissioner, and punishments intendant was to recommend three officials of his circuit with proven conduct and administration, to prepare for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, each pacifier, transport chief, and judicial commissioner was to name three proven subordinates for promotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗任兩府者，許舉內外官。

translations.literal: Those who had served in the Two Departments might recommend inner and outer officials.
translations.idiomatic: Former Two-Department ministers could nominate officials inside and outside court.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，詔轉運司，凡鄰州饑而輒閉糶者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Day dingchou, edict: transport offices—wherever a neighboring prefecture was hungry and grain sales were closed, it was to be prosecuted as violation of edict.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, hoarding grain from starving neighbors was made a statutory offense.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，放宮女二百十四人。

translations.literal: Day xinmao: two hundred fourteen palace women were released.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, 214 palace women were released.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁未，放宮女二百三十六人。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dingwei: two hundred thirty-six palace women were released.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, dingwei: 236 palace women were released.

sentences.zh: 八月乙亥，策制舉人。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yihai: policy examination for classical recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, yihai: special-recruitment candidates faced the policy exam.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬申，朝饗景靈宮。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day renshen: morning feast at Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, renshen: the court feasted at Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，大袷於太廟，大赦。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: great collective offering at the imperial temple; great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the imperial temple received the great collective rite and a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 詔諸路監司察士有學行為鄉里所推者，同長吏以聞。

translations.literal: Edict: circuit commissioners were to investigate scholars of learning and conduct esteemed in their districts; together with magistrates they were to report.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissioners were to report locally esteemed scholars with magistrates.

sentences.zh: 民父母年八十以上，復其一丁。

translations.literal: Where parents were eighty or older, one corvée laborer per household was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Households with parents over eighty lost one corvée draft.

sentences.zh: 復益州為成都府，并州為太原府。

translations.literal: Yizhou was restored as Chengdu prefecture; Bingzhou as Taiyuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou became Chengdu prefecture again; Bingzhou became Taiyuan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，加恩百官。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: additional favor to officials.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, officials received extra favors.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚子，汝南郡王允讓薨。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day gengzi: Prince of Runan Yun Rang died.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, gengzi: Prince of Runan Yun Rang died.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁丑，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day dingchou: a white rainbow spanned the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, dingchou: a white rainbow crossed the sun.

sentences.zh: 是歲，唃廝囉來貢。

translations.literal: That year, Gusiluo came to tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gusiluo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月辛卯朔，白虹貫日，太白犯歲星。

translations.literal: Year five, spring, first month, day xinmao new moon: a white rainbow spanned the sun; Venus transgressed Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 5, new moon xinmao: a white rainbow crossed the sun and Venus overtook Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 己亥，錄劉繼元後。

translations.literal: Day jihai: descendants of Liu Jiyuan were recorded in the register.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Liu Jiyuan’s descendants were entered in the register.

sentences.zh: 二月壬戌，錄系囚。

translations.literal: Second month, day renxu: prisoners were reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, renxu: prisoners were reviewed.

sentences.zh: 三月壬辰，詔禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: Third month, day renchen, edict: Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, renchen: the Ministry of Rites examinations were ordered.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，劉沆薨。

translations.literal: Day guisi: Liu Kang died.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Liu Kang died.

sentences.zh: 乙未，歲星晝見。

translations.literal: Day yiwei: Jupiter was visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Jupiter appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔以蝗澇相仍，敕轉運使、提點刑獄督州縣振濟，仍察不稱職者。

translations.literal: Day renzi, edict: because locusts and floods followed one another, transport commissioners and punishments intendants were ordered to supervise prefectures and counties in relief and still to investigate the incompetent.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, locusts and floods ordered transport and judicial chiefs to relieve counties and purge the incompetent.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸未，程戡罷，以孫抃為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day guimao: Cheng Zhan was removed; Sun Bian was made vice military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, guimao: Cheng Zhan fell and Sun Bian became deputy military director.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，命近臣同三司議均稅。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: close ministers were ordered jointly with the Three Departments to discuss equalizing the tax.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, intimate ministers and the Three Departments were to debate tax equalization.

sentences.zh: 五月戊子朔，京師民疫，選醫給藥以療之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuzi new moon: epidemic struck the capital populace; physicians were selected to dispense medicine for treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, new moon wuzi: capital epidemic brought selected physicians to treat the people.

sentences.zh: 己丑，京師地震。

translations.literal: Day jichou: the capital region had an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the capital region shook.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔三司置寬恤民力司。

translations.literal: Day dingyou, edict: the Three Departments were to establish an Office to Broaden Relief of Popular Burdens.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the Three Departments created an office to ease popular burdens.

sentences.zh: 己酉，王安石召入為三司度支判官。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: Wang Anshi was summoned and made revenue-section judge of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Wang Anshi entered court as Three Departments revenue judge.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，錄系囚，降罪一等，徒以下釋之。

translations.literal: Day dingsi: prisoners were reviewed; crimes were reduced one degree; penal servants and below were released.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, prisoners were reviewed, cut one grade, and penal servants went free.

sentences.zh: 六月乙丑，詔戒上封告訐人罪或言赦前事，及言事官彈劾小過不關政體者。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day yichou, edict: warning against sealed memorials that denounced others’ crimes or spoke of matters before amnesty, and against remonstrance officials impeaching petty faults unrelated to state policy.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, yichou: sealed denunciations, pre-amnesty tales, and petty remonstrance impeachments were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，遣官分行天下，訪寬恤民力事。

translations.literal: Day yihai: officials were sent through the empire to inquire into measures to broaden relief of popular burdens.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, empire-wide envoys sought ways to ease popular burdens.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸巳，邕州言交阯與甲峒蠻合兵寇邊，都巡檢宋士堯拒戰，死之，詔發諸州兵討捕。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day guisi: Yong prefecture reported that Jiaozhi and Jiadong barbarians combined forces to raid the border; patrol inspector Song Shiyao resisted battle and died; edict ordered mobilization of troops from various prefectures to pursue and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, guisi: Jiaozhi and Jiadong allies raided Yong; Song Shiyao was killed; troops from many prefectures were ordered out.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔待制、台諫官、正刺史以上各舉諸司使至三班使臣堪將領及行陣戰鬥者三人。

translations.literal: Day bingshen, edict: drafting officials, remonstrators, and regular prefects and above were each to recommend three bureau agents through third-rank agents fit for command and field battle.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, drafters, remonstrators, and prefects each named three agents fit for command and combat.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，翰林學士歐陽修上新修《唐書》。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Hanlin academician Ouyang Xiu presented the newly revised Book of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Ouyang Xiu presented the revised Book of Tang.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔中書門下采端實之士明進諸朝，辨激巧偽者放黜之。

translations.literal: Day gengxu, edict: the Secretariat was to select upright and solid men to advance clearly to court, and identify and dismiss the sharp and crafty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the Secretariat was to promote the upright and expel the clever frauds.

sentences.zh: 八月壬申，詔求逸書。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day renshen, edict: seek lost books.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, renshen: lost books were ordered sought.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，置陝西估馬司。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: the Shaanxi Horse Appraisal Office was established.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the Shaanxi Horse Appraisal Office was created.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，罷諸路同提點刑獄使臣。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: concurrent circuit punishments deputy commissioners were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, concurrent circuit judicial deputies were abolished.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，置江、湖、閩、廣、四川十一路轉運判官。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: transport deputy commissioners were established for eleven circuits—Jiang, Hu, Min, Guang, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, transport deputies were set for eleven circuits from the Yangzi to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jichou: Venus was visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, jichou: Venus appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙酉，深州言野蠶成繭，被于原野。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day yiyou: Shen prefecture reported wild silkworms forming cocoons spread over the open countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, yiyou: Shenzhou reported wild silkworms cocooning across the fields.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛卯，罷內臣寄遷法。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day xinmao: the inner eunuch provisional promotion law was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, xinmao: inner eunuch provisional promotion ended.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，宋庠罷。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: Song Qi was removed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Song Qi was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以曾公亮為樞密使，張昪、孫抃為參知政事，歐陽修、陳升之、趙概為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang was made military affairs commissioner; Zhang Bian and Sun Bian participating administrators; Ouyang Xiu, Chen Shengzhi, and Zhao Gai vice military affairs commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang headed Military Affairs; Zhang Bian and Sun Bian joined the council; Ouyang Xiu, Chen Shengzhi, and Zhao Gai became deputies.

sentences.zh: 十二月己卯，蘇茂州蠻寇邕州。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jimao: Sumao prefecture barbarians raided Yong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jimao: Sumao tribes raided Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，補諸州父老百歲以上者十二人為州助教。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: twelve elders over one hundred years of age in various prefectures were appointed prefectural teaching assistants.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, twelve centenarians were made prefectural teaching assistants.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大食國來貢。

translations.literal: That year, the Dashi state came to tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Arab lands sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月乙未，許兩制與台諫相見。

translations.literal: Year six, spring, first month, day yiwei: drafting officials and remonstrators were permitted to meet one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 6, first month, yiwei: drafting officials and remonstrators could meet.

sentences.zh: 二月丁巳，詔宗室賜名授官者，須年及十五方許轉官。

translations.literal: Second month, day dingsi, edict: imperial clansmen granted names and office had to reach fifteen years of age before transfer in rank was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, dingsi: clansmen named to office could not transfer rank before age fifteen.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔良民子弟或為人誘隸軍籍，自今兩月內，父母訴官者還之。

translations.literal: Day yichou, edict: commoners’ sons sometimes enticed into military registry—within two months from now, where parents appealed to officials, they were to be returned.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, parents had two months to reclaim sons fraudulently enrolled in the army.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，錄系囚，降罪一等，徒以下釋之。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: prisoners were reviewed; crimes were reduced one degree; penal servants and below were released.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, prisoners were reviewed, cut one grade, and penal servants went free.

sentences.zh: 三月己亥，富弼以母喪去位。

translations.literal: Third month, day jihai: Fu Bi left office on his mother’s mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, jihai: Fu Bi left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以富弼母喪，罷大宴。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: because of Fu Bi’s mother’s mourning, the grand feast was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Fu Bi’s mourning cancelled the grand feast.

sentences.zh: 戊申，給西京周廟祭享器服。

translations.literal: Day wushen: ritual vessels and robes for Zhou temple sacrifices in the Western Capital were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Western Capital Zhou temple ritual gear was issued.

sentences.zh: 是月，賜進士、諸科及第同出身二百九十五人。

translations.literal: That month, two hundred ninety-five jinshi and miscellaneous subjects who passed with equal rank were granted office.
translations.idiomatic: That month 295 jinshi and other equal-rank graduates received office.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛酉，詔嶺南官吏死于儂賊而其家流落未能自歸者，所在給食，護送還鄉。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinyou, edict: Lingnan officials who died at the hands of Nong bandits while their families were stranded and unable to return—wherever they were, food was to be provided and escort home arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, xinyou: stranded families of Lingnan officials killed by Nong rebels were fed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，陳升之罷，以包拯為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: Chen Shengzhi was removed; Bao Zheng was made vice military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Chen Shengzhi fell and Bao Zheng became deputy military director.

sentences.zh: 出諫官唐介、趙抃、御史范師道、呂誨。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Tang Jie, Zhao Bian, censor Fan Shidao, and Lü Hui were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrator Tang Jie, Zhao Bian, and censors Fan Shidao and Lü Hui were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五月丙戌，官諸路敦遣行義文學之士七人。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingxu: seven men of upright conduct and literary learning were officially dispatched from various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, bingxu: seven men of learning and integrity were officially dispatched from the circuits.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，錄系囚，降罪一等，徒以下釋之。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: prisoners were reviewed; crimes were reduced one degree; penal servants and below were released.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, prisoners were reviewed, cut one grade, and penal servants went free.

sentences.zh: 分命官錄三京系囚。

translations.literal: Officials were separately appointed to review prisoners in the three capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Separate officers reviewed prisoners in the three capitals.

sentences.zh: 六月壬子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renzi new moon: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, new moon renzi: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Day yichou: Venus was visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Venus appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 壬申，歲星晝見。

translations.literal: Day renshen: Jupiter was visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Jupiter appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以司馬光知諫院，入對。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: Sima Guang was made remonstrance official and entered for audience.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Sima Guang joined the Remonstrance Bureau and faced the throne.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以王安石知制誥。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: Wang Anshi was made drafting official.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Anshi became a drafting official.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙酉，泗州淮水溢。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day yiyou: the Huai River overflowed at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, yiyou: the Huai flooded at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔淮南、江、浙水災，差官體量蠲稅。

translations.literal: Day bingxu, edict: because of floods in Huainan and Jiang-Zhe, officials were sent to assess and remit taxes.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Huainan and Jiang-Zhe floods brought assessors to remit taxes.

sentences.zh: 戊子，錄昭憲皇太后、孝明孝惠孝章淑德皇后家子孫，進秩授官者十有九人。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: descendants of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian and Empresses Xiaoming, Xiaohui, Xiaozhang, and Shude were recorded; nineteen received rank and office.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, nineteen descendants of Zhaoxian and four empresses received rank and office.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔：「台諫為耳目之官，乃聽險陂之人興造飛語，中傷善良，非忠孝之行也。

translations.literal: Day guisi, edict: “Remonstrators and censors are the ears and eyes of government, yet they heed crafty and crooked men who invent flying slander, wounding the good—this is not conduct of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, remonstrators and censors were warned against slander spread by crafty men.

sentences.zh: 中書門下其申儆百工，務敦行實，循而弗改者絀之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat is to warn all offices to pursue solid conduct; those who persist unchanged are to be demoted.”
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was to warn all offices to pursue solid conduct or face demotion.

sentences.zh: 」八月乙亥，策制舉人。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yihai: policy examination for classical recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, yihai: special-recruitment candidates faced the policy exam.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，詔：「諸路刺舉之官，未有以考其賢否，比令有司詳定厥制，其各務祗新書，以稱朕意。

translations.literal: Day dingchou, edict: “Circuit investigating officials have had no means to test worthiness; recently offices were ordered to detail the system—each should respect the new statutes to accord with Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, circuit investigators were told to apply the new merit statutes faithfully.

sentences.zh: 仍令考校轉運、提刑，課績院以新定條目施行。

translations.literal: Still order evaluation of transport and judicial commissioners; the Merit Review Office is to apply the newly fixed articles.”
translations.idiomatic: Transport and judicial chiefs were to be graded under the new Merit Review Office rules.

sentences.zh: 」戊寅，詔州縣長吏有清白不擾而實惠及民者，令本路監司保薦再任，政跡尤異，當加獎擢。

translations.literal: Day wuyin, edict: where prefectural and county magistrates were clean and non-disturbing and truly benefited the people, circuit commissioners were to recommend them for a second term; where administration was especially outstanding, increased reward and promotion were due.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, clean magistrates who truly helped the people could be recommended for reappointment and special promotion.

sentences.zh: 閏月乙酉，復以成都府為劍南西川節度。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day yiyou: Chengdu prefecture was again made Jiannan West Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, yiyou: Chengdu again became Jiannan West military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以韓琦為昭文館大學士，曾公亮同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士，張昪為樞密使。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: Han Qi was made Zhaowen grand academician; Zeng Gongliang associate chief councilor and Jixian grand academician; Zhang Bian military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Han Qi took Zhaowen; Zeng Gongliang joined the council; Zhang Bian headed Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以胡宿為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: Hu Su was made vice military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Hu Su became deputy military director.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬午，定內侍磨勘法。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day renwu: the inner attendant merit-review law was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, renwu: the inner attendant merit-review law was fixed.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔京西、淮、浙、荊湖增置都同巡檢。

translations.literal: Day bingxu, edict: additional chief co-patrol inspectors were established in Jingxi, Huainan, Zhe, and Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Jingxi, Huainan, Zhe, and Jing-Hu gained new chief co-patrol inspectors.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，起復皇侄、前右衛大將軍、岳州團練使宗實為泰州防御使、知宗正寺。

translations.literal: Day renchen: the emperor’s nephew, former Right Guard grand general and Yuezhou regimentation commissioner Zong Shi, was recalled to service as Taizhou defense commissioner and director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the emperor’s nephew Zong Shi was recalled as Taizhou defender and director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 辭以喪，不拜。

translations.literal: He declined on grounds of mourning and did not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He declined on mourning grounds and did not take the post.

sentences.zh: 十一月己巳，許夏國用漢衣冠。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day jisi: the Xia state was permitted to use Han dress and caps.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, jisi: Xia was allowed Han dress and caps.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，賜昭憲皇太后家信陵坊第。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: the Xiling mansion residence was granted to the Zhaoxian empress dowager’s family.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Zhaoxian empress dowager’s kin received the Xiling mansion.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，許康州刺史李樞以己官封贈父母。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: Li Shu, prefect of Kangzhou, was permitted to use his own office to ennoble his parents posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Kangzhou prefect Li Shu could ennoble his parents with his own rank.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙戌，復豐州。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day bingxu: Feng prefecture was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, bingxu: Fengzhou was restored.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，命諸路總管集隨軍功過簿，以備遷補。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: circuit grand commanders were ordered to compile ledgers of military merit and fault for use in promotion and replacement.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, circuit commanders were to keep merit ledgers for promotions.

sentences.zh: 是歲，冬無冰。

translations.literal: That year, winter brought no ice.
translations.idiomatic: That winter there was no ice.

sentences.zh: 占城國獻馴象，安化州蠻來貢。

translations.literal: Champa presented tame elephants; Anhua prefecture barbarians came to tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Champa sent tame elephants; Anhua tribes sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月辛未，復命皇侄宗實為泰州防御使、知宗正寺。

translations.literal: Year seven, spring, first month, day xinwei: the emperor’s nephew Zong Shi was again appointed Taizhou defense commissioner and director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 7, first month, xinwei: Zong Shi was again made Taizhou defender and clan director.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔南郊以太祖配為定制。

translations.literal: Day yihai, edict: at the southern suburban sacrifice Taizu’s accompaniment was made the permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Taizu’s pairing at the southern suburb was fixed as permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 改溫成皇后廟為祠殿。

translations.literal: The temple of Empress Wencheng was changed to a shrine hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wencheng’s temple became a shrine hall.

sentences.zh: 二月己卯朔，更江西鹽法。

translations.literal: Second month, day jimao new moon: Jiangxi salt law was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, new moon jimao: Jiangxi salt regulations were revised.

sentences.zh: 詔開封府市地於四郊，給錢瘞民之不能葬者。

translations.literal: Edict: Kaifeng prefecture was to buy land in the four suburbs and grant cash to bury people unable to afford burial.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng was to buy suburban land and pay to bury the destitute dead.

sentences.zh: 癸未，錄系囚，命官錄被水諸州系囚。

translations.literal: Day guimao: prisoners were reviewed; officials were appointed to review prisoners in flood-stricken prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, prisoners were reviewed and flood counties got separate reviews.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，詔禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinhai, edict: Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, xinhai: the Ministry of Rites examinations were ordered.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，孫抃罷，以趙概參知政事，吳奎為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Day yimao: Sun Bian was removed; Zhao Gai was made participating administrator; Wu Kui vice military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Sun Bian fell; Zhao Gai joined the council; Wu Kui became deputy military director.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以旱，罷大宴。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: because of drought, the grand feast was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, drought cancelled the grand feast.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，祈雨於西太一宮。

translations.literal: Day yichou: rain was prayed for at the Western Supreme Unity palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, rain rites were held at Western Supreme Unity.

sentences.zh: 庚午，謝雨。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: thanksgiving for rain.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the court gave thanks for rain.

sentences.zh: 壬申，徐州彭城、濠州鐘離地生面十餘頃，民皆取食。

translations.literal: Day renshen: at Pengcheng in Xuzhou and Zhongli in Haozhou, flour grew from the ground over more than ten qing; the people all took it for food.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, flour sprouted across ten-plus qing at Xuzhou and Haozhou and people ate it.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬午，頒《嘉祐編敕》。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day renwu: the Jiayou Compiled Statutes were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, renwu: the Jiayou Compiled Statutes were issued.

sentences.zh: 己丑，夏國主諒祚進馬，求賜書，詔賜《九經》，還其馬。

translations.literal: Day jichou: Xia ruler Liangzuo presented horses and requested books; edict granted the Nine Classics and returned the horses.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Liangzuo’s horses bought the Nine Classics; the horses were returned.

sentences.zh: 五月戊午，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuwu: Venus was visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, wuwu: Venus appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 庚午，包拯卒。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: Bao Zheng died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Bao Zheng died.

sentences.zh: 六月丙子朔，歲星晝見。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day bingzi new moon: Jupiter was visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, new moon bingzi: Jupiter appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊申，太白經天。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day wushen: Venus crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, wushen: Venus crossed the heavens.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔季秋有事於明堂。

translations.literal: Day renzi, edict: in late autumn there would be rites at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, late-autumn Bright Hall rites were ordered.

sentences.zh: 八月乙亥朔，出明堂樂章，肄于太常。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yihai new moon: Bright Hall hymn texts were issued and drilled in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, new moon yihai: Bright Hall hymns were issued to the Court of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔以宗實為皇子。

translations.literal: Day jimao, edict: Zong Shi was made imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Zong Shi was made imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 癸未，賜名曙。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the name Shu was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, he was given the name Shu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，奉安真宗御容于壽星觀。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: Zhenzong’s imperial portrait was installed at the Longevity Star Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Zhenzong’s portrait was enshrined at Longevity Star Abbey.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以立皇子告天地宗廟諸陵。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: because the prince was established, Heaven, Earth, the ancestral temple, and the imperial tombs were notified.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, establishing the prince was announced to Heaven, Earth, the temple, and the tombs.

sentences.zh: 九月乙巳朔，以皇子為齊州防御使，進封钜鹿郡公。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day yisi new moon: the prince was made defense commissioner of Qizhou and advanced to Duke of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, new moon yisi: the prince became Qizhou defender and Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 己酉，朝饗景靈宮。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: morning feast at Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, the court feasted at Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，饗太廟。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: feast at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, offerings went to the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，大饗明堂，奉真宗配，大赦。

translations.literal: Day xinhai: great feast at the Bright Hall with Zhenzong as accompaniment; great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Bright Hall rites with Zhenzong paired and a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己未，加恩百官。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: additional favor to officials.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, officials received extra favors.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙亥，皇子表辭所除官，賜詔不允。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day yihai: the prince memorialized declining the offices granted; an edict refusing consent was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, yihai: the prince declined his posts; the throne refused consent.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: a white rainbow spanned the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, a white rainbow crossed the sun.

sentences.zh: 乙未，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Day yiwei: Venus was visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Venus appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔內藏庫、三司共出緡錢一百萬，助糴天下常平倉。

translations.literal: Day bingshen, edict: the inner treasury and Three Departments were jointly to provide one million strings of cash to help purchase grain for the empire’s Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, inner treasury and Three Departments gave one million strings to stock Ever-Normal granaries.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲午，德妃沈氏為貴妃，賢妃苗氏為德妃。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jiawu: Virtuous Consort Shen was made Precious Consort; Worthy Consort Miao was made Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jiawu: Lady Shen became Precious Consort and Lady Miao became Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 丙申，幸龍圖、天章閣，召群臣宗室觀祖宗御書。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: the emperor visited the Longtu and Tianzhang pavilions and summoned ministers and the imperial clan to view the ancestral imperial writings.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, at Longtu and Tianzhang he showed ancestral writings to ministers and kin.

sentences.zh: 又幸寶文閣，為飛白書，分賜從臣。

translations.literal: He also visited the Baowen Pavilion, wrote flying-white script, and distributed it to attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also visited Baowen, wrote flying-white script, and gave pieces to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 作《觀書詩》，命韓琦等屬和，遂宴群玉殿。

translations.literal: He composed the poem “Viewing Books,” ordered Han Qi and others to compose matching lines, and then feasted at the Jade Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His “Viewing Books” poem sent Han Qi and others to match verses, then a feast at Jade Hall.

sentences.zh: 庚子，再召從臣于天章閣觀瑞物，復宴群玉殿。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: attending ministers were again summoned to Tianzhang Pavilion to view auspicious objects, and again feasted at the Jade Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, ministers viewed auspicious objects at Tianzhang and feasted again at Jade Hall.

sentences.zh: 是歲，冬無冰。

translations.literal: That year, winter brought no ice.
translations.idiomatic: That winter there was no ice.

sentences.zh: 占城來貢。

translations.literal: Champa came to tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Champa sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月辛亥，交阯貢馴象九。

translations.literal: Year eight, spring, first month, day xinhai: Jiaozhi presented nine tame elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 8, first month, xinhai: Jiaozhi sent nine tame elephants.

sentences.zh: 二月癸未，帝不豫。

translations.literal: Second month, day guimao: the emperor fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, guimao: the emperor fell ill.

sentences.zh: 甲申，下德音：減天下囚罪一等，徒以下釋之。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: a gracious edict was issued—prisoners empire-wide had sentences reduced one degree; those below penal servitude were released.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, a gracious edict cut all crimes one grade and freed penal servants and below.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，中書、樞密奏事于福寧殿之西閣。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: the Secretariat and Military Affairs reported affairs in the west pavilion of Funing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the Secretariat and Military Affairs met in Funing Hall’s west pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三月戊申，龐籍薨。

translations.literal: Third month, day wushen: Pang Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, wushen: Pang Ji died.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，御內東門幄殿，優賜諸軍緡錢。

translations.literal: Day guihai: he held court in the East Inner Gate canopy hall and generously granted strings of cash to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, at the East Inner Gate canopy hall he lavishly granted pay to the armies.

sentences.zh: 甲子，御延和殿，賜進士、諸科及第同出身三百四十一人。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: he held court at Yanhe Hall and granted jinshi, various-route graduates, and tong chushen three hundred forty-one men.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, at Yanhe Hall he granted degrees to 341 jinshi and other graduates.

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝崩于福寧殿，遺制皇子即皇帝位，皇后為皇太后，喪服以日易月，山陵制度務從儉約。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: the emperor died in Funing Hall; the testamentary decree ordered the prince to ascend the throne immediately, the empress to become empress dowager, mourning garments to count days for months, and mount-tomb rites to insist on thrift.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he died in Funing Hall—testament: the prince reigns at once, the empress becomes dowager, mourning counts days as months, tomb rites stay spare.

sentences.zh: 諡曰神文聖武明孝皇帝，廟號仁宗。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Divine Culture, Sagely Martiality, Bright Filiality; temple name Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name: Divine Culture, Sagely Martiality, Bright Filiality; temple name Renzong.

sentences.zh: 十月甲午，葬永昭陵。

translations.literal: Tenth month, day jiawu: burial at Yongzhao Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, jiawu: buried at Yongzhao.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：仁宗恭儉仁恕，出於天性，一遇水旱，或密禱禁庭，或跣立殿下。

translations.literal: Praise says: Renzong was respectful, frugal, benevolent, and forgiving by nature; whenever flood or drought came, he would secretly pray in the palace or stand barefoot in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: by nature respectful, frugal, and forgiving—in flood or drought he prayed in secret or stood barefoot in the hall.

sentences.zh: 有司請以玉清舊地為御苑，帝曰：「吾奉先帝苑囿，猶以為廣，何以是為？

translations.literal: When officials proposed the old Yuqing site as an imperial park, the emperor said, "I maintain my father’s park and still find it vast—why do this?
translations.idiomatic: When they proposed the old Yuqing grounds for a park, he said, "My father’s park is already vast—why this?

sentences.zh: 」燕私常服浣濯，帷帟衾裯，多用繒絁。

translations.literal: " In private he often wore washed clothes; curtains, bedding, and coverlets were mostly plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: " In private he wore washed clothes and plain silk for curtains and bedding.

sentences.zh: 宮中夜饑，思膳燒羊，戒勿宣索，恐膳夫自此戕賊物命，以備不時之須。

translations.literal: Once at night in the palace he grew hungry and thought of roast lamb, but forbade announcing a request, fearing the kitchen staff would henceforth slaughter living creatures to stock occasional needs.
translations.idiomatic: Hungry at night, he thought of roast lamb but forbade asking, lest the kitchens slaughter stock in advance.

sentences.zh: 大辟疑者，皆令上讞，歲常活千餘。

translations.literal: In capital cases where doubt remained, all were sent up for review; each year more than a thousand lives were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful capital cases went up for review—each year he spared more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 吏部選人，一坐失入死罪，皆終身不遷。

translations.literal: Civil-service candidates whom a single error had caused to be sentenced to death were never promoted for life.
translations.idiomatic: A single death-sentence slip barred civil candidates from promotion for life.

sentences.zh: 每諭輔臣曰：「朕未嘗詈人以死，況敢濫用辟乎！

translations.literal: He often told his chief ministers, "I have never cursed a man with death—how much less would I abuse the death penalty!
translations.idiomatic: He told his ministers, "I never curse men with death—how would I abuse execution!

sentences.zh: 」至於夏人犯邊，御之出境；

translations.literal: " When Xi Xia raided the border, he drove them beyond it;
translations.idiomatic: " Xi Xia raids—he drove them out;

sentences.zh: 契丹渝盟，增以歲幣。

translations.literal: when Khitan violated the covenant, he increased the annual payment.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan covenant-breakers got a higher annual gift.

sentences.zh: 在位四十二年之間，吏治若偷惰，而任事蔑殘刻之人；

translations.literal: Through forty-two years on the throne, official governance seemed negligent, yet those in office were seldom harsh or cruel;
translations.idiomatic: Forty-two years in power: governance seemed slack, yet ministers were rarely cruel;

sentences.zh: 刑法似縱弛，而決獄多平允之士。

translations.literal: penal law seemed lax, yet those deciding cases were mostly fair and even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: law seemed loose, yet judges were mostly fair.

sentences.zh: 國未嘗無弊幸，而不足以累治世之體；

translations.literal: The state never lacked abuses and favoritism, yet not enough to mar the body of a well-governed age;
translations.idiomatic: Favoritism never wrecked the age’s order;

sentences.zh: 朝未嘗無小人，而不足以勝善類之氣。

translations.literal: the court never lacked petty men, yet not enough to overwhelm the spirit of the good.
translations.idiomatic: petty men never drowned the good.

sentences.zh: 君臣上下惻怛之心，忠厚之政，有以培壅宋三百餘年之基。

translations.literal: The sympathetic hearts of ruler and ministers above and below, and policies of generous loyalty, nurtured the foundation of Song’s more than three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Sympathy and loyal forbearance nourished Song’s three-century foundation.

sentences.zh: 子孫一矯其所為，馴致於亂。

translations.literal: When descendants corrected his ways one by one, they slid step by step into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Once heirs reversed his ways, disorder followed step by step.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「為人君，止於仁。

translations.literal: The Classic says, "As a ruler, one stops at benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic: "A ruler rests in benevolence."

sentences.zh: 」帝誠無愧焉。

translations.literal: The emperor truly had no cause for shame.
translations.idiomatic: He truly had nothing to regret.
